end_card: Glass Wall AI · glass-wall-ai.vercel.app · Voice: ElevenLabs

beats.label: A real attack
beats.text: This AI assistant just handed a stranger the names, emails and phone numbers of twenty customers. It took one message.

beats.label: The trick
beats.text: Companies are starting to let AI assistants work directly with their customer data, and these assistants can be talked into things.

beats.label: The Glass Wall
beats.text: Glass Wall fixes that. Think of frosted glass: the AI can see the shape of the data, how many customers, which city, which plan, but never who they are.

beats.label: Codes, not people
beats.text: Every name, email and phone number reaches it as a code. The same person always gets the same code, so the AI can still count and match, without ever knowing who anyone is.

beats.label: No protection
beats.text: Let's try to trick one. Here's a real AI assistant with no protection.

beats.label: The trick
beats.text: Someone pretends to be from the compliance team and asks it to send out every business customer's contact details.

beats.label: Real data leaving
beats.text: It obeys. Red means real personal data just got out.

beats.label: What the stranger got
beats.text: This box shows what the stranger received: real names, emails and phone numbers. For any company, that's a data breach.

beats.label: Wall up
beats.text: Same assistant, same trick, but now the Glass Wall is up.

beats.label: Still trying to help
beats.text: The assistant still tries to help. It even sends the message.

beats.label: Only codes
beats.text: But all it ever had were codes, so the stranger gets nothing useful.

beats.label: Blocked by the database
beats.text: And when it tries to sneak around the wall and read the customer list directly, the database simply says no.

beats.label: 60 tricks, every setup
beats.text: We didn't try it just once. We threw sixty different tricks at four different AI models, hundreds of times.

beats.label: Without the wall
beats.text: Without the wall, about three out of four tricks worked. Just telling the AI "please be careful" helped, but some tricks still got through.

beats.label: Zero leaks
beats.text: With the Glass Wall: zero. Not one real name, email or phone number got out.

beats.label: Still useful
beats.text: And everyday questions, like counting customers per plan, still got the right answer.

beats.label: The trade-off
beats.text: It isn't magic. Questions about the hidden details themselves, like how many customers use a certain email provider, can't be answered.

beats.label: A false alarm, shown openly
beats.text: And we publish every single run, including the few times our own quick checker raised a false alarm.

beats.label: Inside the database
beats.text: For the technical folks: the wall lives inside the database itself, not in the AI's instructions, so no clever message can talk it out of it.

beats.label: MCP
beats.text: Any AI agent can connect to it through MCP, the standard way agents plug into tools.
Try to break it yourself, the link is below. Glass Wall: AI sees the shape of the data, never the people in it.
